ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-10.recent: Euro-area households now expect 3.1% inflation, up from 3%, while loan obstacles already hit 7% of euro zone firms. The council is weighing expectations drifting up against credit that is already tightening, with Lagarde having credited a bond selloff and a December hike in view, and France's bond rout testing how much tightening a debt-strained member can bear.

boj-2026-10.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-10.recent: The question before this board is whether Japan's inflation is now wage-driven, the kind a central bank can tighten against, rather than imported through a weak yen. The yen's climb to a one-month high at 156.28 per dollar, on AI doubts, has eased some of that imported pressure.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-11.recent: The committee meets after inflation and borrowing data framed the chancellor's Budget challenge, which puts the price of money and the cost of government borrowing in front of it at once. The decision settles what Bank Rate does next for the borrowers and savers who carry it.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-12.recent: The first meeting after the US midterms settles whether the Fed's first hike in three years was a one-off. Kevin Warsh has withheld guidance, calling AI a shock to the economy, while oil-driven inflation from the Iran war splits a committee that TD Securities expected to post 3 dissents against its last hold.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of leaders of the world's largest economies, hosted by the member holding the rotating presidency. Its members produce about 85% of global output, and its communiqué sets shared lines on trade and debt.
g20-2026-miami.recent: Trump has snubbed South Africa, and Merz has urged him to invite it to Miami. Zelenskyy is eyeing a meeting with the US and Russia on the sidelines, while Putin has floated a three-way summit with Trump and Xi that would seat no Ukrainian.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-12.recent: Euro-area households now expect 3.1% inflation, up from 3%, while the ECB's own survey finds loan obstacles hitting 7% of euro zone firms. Lagarde has pointed to the bond selloff that hit France, and December weighs a hike against credit that is already tightening on its own.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: The committee decides with inflation and borrowing data already framing the chancellor's Budget challenge, so it weighs price pressure against a government whose own borrowing costs move with its rate. The decision settles what households and the Treasury pay for credit into the new year.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-12.recent: Tokyo is now weighing whether inflation is becoming wage-driven, the question that decides whether a rate already at a 31-year high goes further. The board also meets with markets fully pricing a December Fed hike, which would widen the gap the yen trades on. The yen's latest lift, to a one-month high at 156.28 per dollar, came from AI doubts, not policy.

fred-us-pce-2026-10-29.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's monthly report on personal income and spending, carrying the PCE price index the Federal Reserve targets at 2%. It moves rate expectations, Treasury yields and the dollar.
fred-us-pce-2026-10-29.recent: The Bureau of Economic Analysis releases the latest US PCE figures, settling how fast the prices households pay rose last month and whether their spending kept pace with their income.

fred-us-gdp-2026-10-29.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's quarterly estimate of US gross domestic product, first published about a month after each quarter ends and revised twice after. Treasury yields, the dollar and Fed expectations move on it.
fred-us-gdp-2026-10-29.recent: The release lands in the same week the Fed sets rates, at a meeting previewed as a hawkish pause. That makes it the broadest measure the committee and markets have of how the US economy fared over the quarter just ended.

fred-us-jobs-report-2026-11-06.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly employment report, released on the first Friday of most months, counting jobs added, the unemployment rate and wage growth. Treasury yields, the dollar and Fed rate bets reprice within minutes.
fred-us-jobs-report-2026-11-06.recent: This release reports a month of payroll hiring, the unemployment rate and average hourly pay, along with revisions to the two months before it. It settles how much the labor market added or shed over that month, the reading rate-setters weigh against inflation.
